 Sreenidi Deccan Seek Redemption Against Unbeaten-at-Home FC Bengaluru United in IFL Clash
 Sreenidi Deccan Seek Redemption Against Unbeaten-at-Home FC Bengaluru United in IFL Clash
 By IndiaSportsHub Desk View author profile 18 Nov 2026 Football Credit IFL Like Comment Listen Save Share Sreenidi Deccan FC will look to put their recent defeat behind them when they take on FC Bengaluru United in Match 16 of the Indian Football League 2026-27 at the Bangalore Football Stadium on Wednesday, November 18.  
 With both teams level on four points after three matches, the encounter offers an opportunity to move into the top three and strengthen their early-season position. Kick-off is scheduled for 6:30 PM IST. The match will be telecast live on DD Sports and streamed on the Unite8 YouTube Channel, Z5 and WAVES App. 
 The contest brings together two sides approaching the fixture from different perspectives. Promoted FC Bengaluru United are building confidence in their debut Star Cement IFL campaign and remain unbeaten at home, while Sreenidi Deccan are seeking a response after a narrow loss to Shillong Lajong. 
 Head coach Nallappan Mohanraj's FC Bengaluru United currently occupy fifth place with four points from three matches. Their latest outing, a 2-2 draw against Real Kashmir FC, demonstrated the team's ability to remain competitive even when chasing the game. 
 Bengaluru fell behind early but found an equaliser through Colombian playmaker Maikol Andres Herrera Casseres, whose right-footed curling strike from distance brought the hosts back into the contest. After conceding again, the team continued to push and were rewarded in the 90th minute when Under-22 centre-back Abdul Hannan rose to head home the equaliser. 
 Mohanraj was pleased with the character his players displayed, although he admitted that securing all three points at home would have been the preferred outcome. 
 "The way we came back into the game, being 2-1 down and scoring in the 90th minute to get a point, we have to accept that fact because everyone worked together and fought well," Mohanraj said. "As a coach at home, I would have liked to take all three points. But the way we fought for that one point made me very happy, and the boys deserved it." 
 The Bengaluru coach also acknowledged the challenge of adapting to the intensity of the top division, particularly for players experiencing this level of competition for the first time. He described Sreenidi Deccan as an experienced opponent but insisted that his side would approach the match with full commitment. 
 Midfielder Lalramdinsanga Ralte echoed that confidence, emphasising the importance of maintaining belief until the final whistle. The late equaliser against Real Kashmir, he said, reinforced the squad's determination to keep fighting regardless of the scoreline. 
 Sreenidi Deccan seek response after Shillong defeat 
 Sreenidi Deccan are sixth in the standings, also with four points, but trail Bengaluru United narrowly on goals scored. A victory on Wednesday would allow the Deccan Warriors to move ahead of their opponents and revive their push towards the top of the table. 
 Spanish head coach Antonio Rueda's side suffered a 2-1 defeat against Shillong Lajong in their previous fixture. After conceding early in the second half, Sreenidi responded through substitute Nicolas Morinigo, who headed home in the 72nd minute following tactical adjustments from the coaching staff. 
 However, Shillong scored again late in the match to take all three points. Sreenidi came close to rescuing a draw in the closing stages, but captain David Castañeda saw his looping header cleared off the goal line. 
 Rueda believes the team must learn from the narrow defeat and avoid repeating the mistakes that have cost them points. 
 "Losing is never interesting. We just have to learn from our mistakes and not repeat them," Rueda said. "We had chances, but we conceded one more goal than them. The league is very competitive. We know that any mistake could cost us points. We have to play at 100 per cent for every minute of the match." 
 The Sreenidi coach also recognised the progress made by Bengaluru United since their promotion, describing them as a team with interesting players and a difficult system to break down. He expects a close contest and stressed the importance of maintaining belief in his team's project and potential. 
 Playmaker Adriano Castanheira underlined the visitors' motivation to finish their demanding road trip with three points. He acknowledged the difficulty of playing away but pointed out that every match carries importance at this early stage of the season. 
 Much of Wednesday's contest could be decided in midfield , where both sides possess players capable of influencing the tempo and direction of the game. Bengaluru United's midfield options include Jojo Zaihmingthanga, Ribhav Sardesai and Maikol Herrera, whose attacking contribution was evident against Real Kashmir. They will face a significant test against Sreenidi's experienced core, featuring Pronay Halder and Adriano Castanheira. 
 The defensive battle will be equally important. Bengaluru's central defenders, including the in-form Abdul Hannan, will need to remain alert to the movement of Sreenidi captain and striker David Castañeda, as well as Morinigo's aerial threat. 
 For Bengaluru, maintaining their unbeaten home record would reinforce the confidence built over the opening fixtures. For Sreenidi, the priority is to turn competitive performances into points and avoid another costly late setback. 
 With both teams level on four points, Wednesday's meeting carries importance beyond the immediate result. Three points would provide either side with a valuable opportunity to climb the standings and establish momentum in the early stages of the 2026-27 campaign.
